docstring_samples: CATCHES: lexer implementations that produce incorrect token types, values, or structure compared to reference implementation; regressions in tokenization logic for any of the 320+ supported language lexers.

CATCHES: implementations that ignore --profile flag, create empty profile,
produce invalid pprof format, or fail to flush profile data on normal exit —
'go tool pprof' must recognize the file as valid (exit 0).

CATCHES: lexer implementations that produce incorrect token types, values, or structure compared to reference implementation; regressions in tokenization logic for any of the 320+ supported language lexers.

CATCHES: lexer implementations that produce incorrect token types, values, or structure compared to reference implementation; regressions in tokenization logic for any of the 320+ supported language lexers.

CATCHES: implementations that produce truncated help, omit flag listings,
change the description text, or remove sections — exact golden match detects
any output deviation from the reference implementation.

CATCHES: implementations that reject or mishandle underscores in note names,
treat underscores as special characters, or fail to create the exact filename.
Test creating a folder with spaces in name.
Test note with very long name.
Test entering a vault that doesn't exist.
Test -h flag for each command.

CATCHES: implementations that fail on filenames with spaces (treating them as
delimiters), quotes (shell escaping bugs), parentheses (regex metacharacter issues),
or brackets (glob expansion bugs).

Golden files: special_chars.golden -- renaming files with spaces, apostrophes,
parentheses, brackets, hyphens, underscores.
CATCHES: implementations that don't honor -w flag in regex mode to allow overwriting all files to same name

Externalized from: tests/regex_test.rs::test_regex_subdir_max_depth
Upward trace: main -> cli -> regex subdir mode with --depth and --max-depth.
Downward trace: same observable filesystem changes for this layout.
Test sort in quiet mode.

CATCHES: implementations that ignore the -d flag and operate in the current directory,
or that fail to resolve relative paths correctly when -d is specified, resulting in
file not found errors or operations in the wrong location.

Golden files: sort_with_dir_flag.golden -- output when operating in subdir

CATCHES: implementations that don't store previous results, don't recognize
'_' as a special variable, evaluate '_' as zero or undefined, or fail to update
the previous answer storage after each evaluation — '5*5' then '_ + 10' must
produce 25 then 35.

Golden files: 
    state_before_underscore.golden -- screen after '5*5'
    state_underscore_usage.golden -- screen after '_ + 10'
Test deg function converts radians to degrees.

CATCHES: implementations that don't define constant pi or use wrong value,
would produce π ≠ 3.141592653... instead of the mathematical constant.
Test nth root function
Test base and fix together.
Test .secretsignore with both file patterns and [secrets] section.
Test with nested .gitignore files.
Test detection of modern npm tokens.
Test file with unicode content.
Test --strict-ignore flag respects .secretsignore for paths.
Test stdin with relative paths.
Test NNN_ORDER environment variable.
Test file:// with root path.
Test opening a specific file.

CATCHES: implementations that fail to handle non-executable scripts gracefully,
crash when given invalid command paths, don't show appropriate error messages for
permission denied, or incorrectly execute non-executable files.

Golden files: none (verifies error handling behavior)
Test PID list with spaces.
Test that color mode contains ANSI codes.
Test LC_ALL environment variable.
Run htop for many iterations with default config.
Test no-color mode produces different output.

CATCHES: implementations that accept 'match name { }' syntax without error,
when match groups are non-capturing and should not allow identifiers, or
implementations that silently ignore the identifier instead of rejecting it.
Test reading from stdin with explicit '-' argument.
Externalized from: crates/melody_compiler/tests/mod.rs::assertion_test
Test not with whitespace symbol.
Externalized from: crates/melody_cli/tests/mod.rs::cli_stdin_stdout_no_hyphen_test

CATCHES: implementations that allow modification of individual bytes in fixed bytes
arrays - they'd either not error or emit wrong message missing 'single bytes in fixed
bytes arrays cannot be modified'.

Targets: checker.rs lines 258-261 (fixed bytes index lvalue check)
Golden files: fixed_bytes_index_assign.sol, fixed_bytes_index_assign_err.txt

CATCHES: implementations where order of --emit values affects output structure —
--emit hashes,abi must produce same contract data as --emit abi,hashes (order may differ).
Test compilation with missing file that doesn't exist.

Externalized from: tests/ui/<suite>/<name>.sol (and optional per-revision snapshots).

Upward trace: executable [FLAGS...] [INPUT]..., where FLAGS come from `//@ compile-flags`.
Downward trace:
  - If a snapshot `.stdout` exists, assert stdout matches.
  - If a snapshot `.stderr` exists, assert stderr diagnostics contain expected markers.
  - Otherwise, parse-only smoke test.

CATCHES: Implementations that fail to process escape sequences in import paths
correctly. The path "./test\ttab.sol" contains \t which should be interpreted
as a tab character per Solidity string literal escaping rules. The error message
must show the interpreted path with the tab, not the literal \t.

Golden files:
    escape_sequences_error.golden -- error showing escaped tab character (stderr)
CATCHES: spec implementations that fail to correctly parse argc specifications for symbol scenarios

CATCHES: implementations that fail to create Argcfile.sh, create it with wrong content
(missing shebang, eval line, or set -e), or produce incorrect stdout message — exact match
on both stdout message and file content ensures correctness.
CATCHES: implementations that don't properly handle compgen functionality
CATCHES: validate implementations that fail to correctly handle arg_unknown scenarios

CATCHES: implementations that don't properly handle --argc-script-path when no 
Argcfile exists in the directory tree — they'd either crash, return an empty string, 
or produce a generic error instead of the specific "Argcfile not found." message.
